Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and inherited rollout evidence. I’ll also apply the required fish-control bookshelf protocol and the wake-visual inspection skill before proposing or editing the single candidate.

The contract confirms that the candidate must remain non-empty, notes must precede the policy edit, and guidance must gain a durable evidence-backed lesson. I’m now anchoring the visual comparison in the inherited observations, metrics, diagnostics, policy variants, and bookshelf primitives.

All four sampled rollouts satisfy the direct uniform still-water initialization and capture successfully; there is no semantic failure in this sample. I’ll therefore compare the best finite candidate with the slowest/worst-scoring sibling, plus the two intermediate actuator-sharing variants, and treat “failure” as the documented residual yaw/load problem rather than inventing a failed termination.

The inherited parent’s unevaluated hypothesis now has a completed result: its pressure-gated actuator sharing retained capture but regressed mean distance to `2.435590L` and score to `-0.537642`, worse than both the progress baseline and blanket allocator. I’m inspecting that rollout directly and will use it as the informative negative case; this is the key reusable lesson the current guidance does not yet contain.

The candidate hypothesis is now evidence-led: restore the fastest v24 course-directed carrier and add one new feasibility mechanism—a one-sided joint-speed envelope that smoothly fades only acceleration pushing an already-near-limit joint farther outward, while preserving inward braking. This targets the persistent `95%`-of-speed-limit exposure (`19.76%` anterior, `9.37%` posterior in v24) without adding another failed terminal cue arbiter or changing the physical limits. I’ll record this diagnosis and bookshelf transfer before touching the policy, as required.

The policy now preserves v24’s steering and wake-producing carrier, changing only the final command-feasibility layer. I’m checking that the diff contains no residual half-cycle logic and that every new parameter is declared before I update the durable guidance with the parent’s falsified pressure-gating result.

The durable guidance now records the parent’s concrete negative result: lower acceleration exposure did not translate to better course behavior or score, so later workers should not treat command pressure as a steering selector. It also states the falsification boundary for the new speed-envelope hypothesis without claiming this unevaluated candidate succeeds. Next I’m running the prescribed checker and lightweight policy-contract probes—no CFD.

The guidance checker passes. The prescribed literal `julia` command is unavailable on this shell (the same environment limitation noted by prior workers), so I’m locating the workspace’s Julia wrapper and will run the identical non-CFD contract probe through it, then run the boundary/schema guard.

The local checks pass, including the speed-envelope invariants, Julia policy contract, parameter ownership, and solver boundary. I’m now invoking the workspace’s prescribed check-runner for an independent final contract audit, as required by `README.md`; it will not run CFD.

The configured check-runner could not start because its pinned model is unavailable in this account environment. I’ve already completed its exact commands locally; I’m using an equivalent independent agent audit as the fallback so the prescribed validation is still covered.

The fallback independent audit passes all three required checks and confirms no sibling candidate was created; the pre-existing naive-carrier reference is unchanged. I’m adding that non-CFD verification to the provenance note and performing one final materiality check.

Completed exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl): restores v24 and adds one-sided joint-speed viability projection.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md): visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, hypothesis, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md): records the parent pressure-gating negative result and reusable speed-boundary lesson.

All non-CFD checks pass: guidance materiality, Julia contract, parameter schema, boundary guard, reflection equivariance, and one-candidate rule. No CFD was run.
